explanation: Fires on the function word that completes a vague or hedging fixed phrase: 'of' in 'some kind/type of', 'not' in 'whether or not', and 'way' in 'some way / in whatever way / in every way / in a complex way'. The preceding context decides it; the same tokens elsewhere fire weakly or not at all ('a better way', 'understanding of' only reach about 20%).

A mixture. It fires strongly at fixed slots in boilerplate text, such as 'the' in 'Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License")', 'governing' in 'language governing permissions', 'version' after license names, and 'trademark of', plus code-header tokens ('super', 'Object.defineProperty', 'def readme'). It also fires at scattered unrelated prose tokens (a closing parenthesis after an abbreviation, 'maker of', 'HOWLS'). There is no single rule.

Fires most strongly on the ' +' of a timezone offset that follows a long run of zeros in a timestamp (e.g. '0000000 +0800'), and fairly strongly on a period or newline after such zero runs. Elsewhere it fires weakly (about 25-40%) on miscellaneous tokens: 'en' in html lang="en", word pieces inside names or foreign words, and code tokens.
Mostly fires on structural code or markup tokens near the start of a file or statement: 'package' after a generated-code header, 'import (' in Go, ' rel' in '

A mixture with no shared trigger: word pieces in Cyrillic text, path pieces in #include lines, variables in math expressions ('*z', '*h'), the second piece of a first name that repeats a page title (e.g. 'Miche|le', 'Rach|ael' at the start of a biography), and assorted code tokens ('.then', 'Objective'). It is hard to predict.

Fires on the token that completes a sentence-level discourse or transition idiom that frames what comes next: 'to name a few', 'To add to that', 'One thing is certain', 'First off', 'What's more', 'That's ...', 'On top of', 'The best part is', 'All that said', 'As far as'. It depends on context; the same words in ordinary use fire weakly or not at all.

A mixture. It fires strongly on 'of' in the copyright notice 'Use of this source code is ...' and on terms-of-use wording ('By using this site', 'Your use of this website'). It also fires on word pieces inside technical or scientific terms ('Lag|rang|ian', 'non-Ab|elian', 'sulf|id|ic', 'hypocyclo|idal'), on 'area under' (the curve), on digits in long numbers, and on code whitespace.

A mixture of unrelated contexts: indentation whitespace in code, '+' and spaces in arithmetic word problems ('Let c = 199 + ...'), 'P' in reported p-values, commas in C++ template argument lists, and occasional 'the'/'as' in plain prose. There is no clear single trigger.

Fires at assorted tokens inside highly formulaic text: legal opinions ('unanimously that', 'questions of law', 'NOTATION'), license notices ('this notice', 'copyright notice'), species stubs ('a species of moth', 'gastropod'), and also code tokens ('extends Component', '&&'). These have no common token-level property, so it reads as a mixture.

Tends to fire on a word piece inside a less common technical word or proper name (e.g. 'Lat|v|ian', 'ghre|lin', 'therm|oplast|ics', 'nor|ve|gicus', 'gall|bl|adder', 'acc|ret|ed', 'nonpath|ogenic'). It also fires on many unrelated whole words ('Highway', 'writ', 'set', 'look', 'American', 'data class'), so it is a loose mixture.

Fires on a determiner or adjective that modifies an upcoming noun naming a place or destination: 'the right place', 'a desired location', 'the appropriate area', 'the correct place', 'a particular place', 'his favorite city', 'the only one', and especially 'other' in 'other cities/realms/materials'. It fires strongly only when the phrase points to a place or option among alternatives.

Fires on word pieces of technical names for laboratory or clinical methods, such as 'spect|rom|etry', 'N|MR', 'def|ibr|illation', 'cyt|ometry', and 'CM|R'. It also fires on unrelated code and shell tokens ('-p' in 'mysql -u user -p', '.toString', 'xmlns', 'private:', '#include "'). These are two unrelated groups.

Often fires on 'in' or 'of' after a noun or verb where it introduces a containing location or whole ('passed in', 'a fire in', 'entered in that cell', 'a driver in', 'part of', 'state of', 'body of'). It also fires on unrelated tokens such as place-name pieces ('Cham|oli'), code arguments ('(root', ':url'), and 'IANS' or 'news'. Prepositions in other uses fire weakly.

Mostly fires on tokens inside code: function names and argument starts ('paste0', 'make_pair(x', 'fields[k'), separators, indentation, and docblock '@'. It also fires on 'per' in rate expressions in prose ('$180,000 per session', '1.5 per 100', 'beats per measure'). The two groups are unrelated, and the code part has no single trigger.
